new.n: Convict's robbery gold on Light House Hill, Grand Haven (1874 tale; 1899 hunt)
new.pl: Light House Hill: the dune bluff on the south side of the Grand River mouth where the 1839 and 1855 lighthouses stood (not Dewey Hill across the river)
new.st: About 1874 a Jackson prison convict told Ottawa County coroner Curtis W. Gray he had buried several thousand dollars of robbery gold 'in the hill immediately back of the light house', beside a described tree on Light House Hill. Gray and Marshal Ike Sanford dug and found nothing. In October 1899 N. Stebbins and Col. William C. Baty of Pueblo, Colorado, searched the hill with 'metal instruments'; five days later the Tribune wrote that 'many persons in town believe that Col. Baty the treasure hunter found the gold he was searching after.' Pin is approximate (the bluff), not the spot itself.
new.t: Two 1899 issues of the local paper plus the statewide wire give the place and named searchers; the 1874 confession is second-hand, and Baty's find was never confirmed. The old lighthouses were gone after the 1905 pier lights. Park and Coast Guard ground: look-only.
